summary: The Status.Update assertions show that a later non-OK status replaces the first error, then an OK status clears it. The header documents first-error retention, but the current implementation of Status::Update is not included, so the repair location and overload behavior need confirmation.
hypotheses: Status::Update(const Status&) assigns the new status without checking whether the receiver is already non-OK.
Status::Update(Status&&) assigns or moves the new status without preserving an existing non-OK status; this may also let an OK rvalue clear an error.
